text: Fern's knee operation is finally on Thursday after eighteen months on the waiting list. Her husband Gareth is taking the week off to look after her, and she's been told no driving for six weeks afterwards. She's worried about going stir crazy, so I should lend her that box set and maybe pop round with lunch the following Monday.
Lior ran the Cardiff half on Sunday and knocked four minutes off his best time. He's already talking about a full marathon next spring.
Natasha is pregnant again! Due in April. She said the morning sickness has been worse than with her first.
Remind me to text Dafydd the night before his hernia op to wish him well. It's next Tuesday at the Heath.
Kerry's daughter Anika has her grade five piano recital on Saturday afternoon. Kerry is more nervous than Anika is.

Lwazi said his dad had a mild stroke last week and is still in hospital. His speech is coming back slowly, but he can't use his left hand yet. Lwazi is flying out to Durban on Friday to be with him and his stepmum, and doesn't know yet when he'll be back. He sounded wrung out. Work have been decent about it, at least.
Christening for Afua and Jamal's little boy is on the 9th. I'm doing the cake.
Chris is playing in the cup semi-final this weekend. Should ask him on Monday how it went.
Irina had her twelve-week scan this morning and everything looks fine. She's telling her parents at dinner tomorrow.
Ayo got a hip replacement in the summer and is finally walking without the stick. Says he wants to do the Great North Run next year, which seems ambitious.
Nadia and her partner Callum had the baby on Wednesday night! A girl, Fern, 7lb 2oz. Need to send flowers once they're home.
Lachlan's band have a gig at the Moon on Friday. He asked if I'd come; I said yes.
Nasser's wife is having a C-section on Monday. He's nervous about it and asked if I could cover his shifts that week.
Laura's play opens on Thursday and runs until Saturday. She's playing Lady Macbeth and is terrified about the sleepwalking scene. Don't forget to text her good luck that afternoon.
Book my own blood test before the end of the month. Surgery said mornings are quieter.
Oliver's grandma, her Nana, came out of hospital yesterday after her fall. She's staying with his mum for a couple of weeks while her wrist heals.

Mihai got through to the regional final of the chess championship. It's in Birmingham in a fortnight, over two days, and the winner goes to nationals in March. He's been studying openings every night after work and his girlfriend Irina says he talks about the Sicilian in his sleep. He's quietly confident but doesn't want a fuss made.
Malik's cataract surgery got cancelled again because of staffing. They've moved it to the 28th instead.

Siobhan is expecting twins. She found out at the scan on Tuesday and is still in shock, because twins don't run in either family. Her partner Anders laughed for about five minutes and then went very quiet. They're going to have to sell the Fiesta and get something bigger before the spring. Her mum has already started knitting two of everything.
Anders came off his bike in the triathlon on Sunday and broke his collarbone. Surgery is tomorrow. I should check in with him the day after.
Amara's son Finn started swimming lessons and loves them. Apparently he wants goggles with sharks on for his birthday.

Valentina's choir concert is next Wednesday at St Mary's, starting at half seven. She's doing a solo in the second half, the Pie Jesu, and has been practising it in the car every morning. Her husband Bogdan and their kids are coming, and she asked whether I'd sit with them. Bring tissues, apparently. Wear something warm too, as the church heating is broken.
Bogdan has been off work for three weeks with his back. He's seeing a specialist on Thursday and hopes they'll finally book the injection.
Miriam's baby shower was meant to be this Saturday but it's been called off; she's been put on bed rest. Her sister Fern is organising a small visit instead.
Louis is running the Bath 10k on Sunday morning in a dinosaur costume for the children's hospital. Must sponsor him before then.
Hoang said the twins' christening went beautifully. His mother-in-law cried through the whole thing.
Called Gareth. His mum's operation went well and she's being discharged on Friday, but she'll need someone with her for the first few nights. He and his sister Kerry are taking turns.
Jamal has his audition for the conservatoire on the 14th. He's been practising six hours a day and isn't sleeping much. Text him the morning of it.
Lwazi's partner Afua is due any day now. Bag's packed, he says, but the car seat still isn't fitted.
Natasha's husband Chris had his gallbladder out yesterday. He's home already and annoyed he can't lift anything.
Ask Irina how her brother Ayo's boxing match went. It was on Saturday night in Leeds.
Kerry loves amateur dramatics and has been in every panto in town for ten years. This year she's the dame.
Dentist moved to next Tuesday at 9:15. Need to leave work early the day before to get the car back from the garage.
Dafydd's little girl had her tonsils out on Monday. He says she's mostly been living on ice lollies and Bluey since.
Anika passed her grade five with distinction! Kerry sent a video of her playing it.

Spent ages on the phone with Lior. His mum, Mrs Garcia, has her heart bypass on Tuesday the 3rd. He's flying back from Tel Aviv the day before and staying the whole week. She's frightened but the surgeon sounds very good. I'll drop a meal round to his flat the weekend after, and remind me to call him on the Wednesday to see how it went.
Lachlan and Siobhan are coming to the gig with me on Friday. Meeting at the pub beforehand.
Need to buy a christening present for baby Louis. The service is on Sunday the 16th and Nadia said they'd love a silver spoon or something engraved.
Fern is recovering well. Physio twice a week now and she managed the stairs on her own yesterday.
Malik is a huge Leeds Rhinos fan and goes to every home game with his son.
Nasser's baby arrived early, at 34 weeks, and is in the neonatal unit for now. Both doing OK, but he's exhausted. I should drop round some food on Thursday.
Valentina said her dad's prostate results come back next Friday. She's trying not to think about it until then.
Miriam had the baby! A boy, Oliver, born on Sunday morning after a long labour. They're staying in another night and going home Tuesday.
Nothing much to note. Lovely long walk with Oliver and his dog Biscuit, who is getting very grey round the muzzle.

Callum's under-twelves team won the county cup final yesterday. His son Louis scored the winner in extra time, a header from a corner, and was carried off on everyone's shoulders. Callum says he hasn't stopped grinning since and slept in his medal. They've got a celebration barbecue at the club next Saturday afternoon and the whole family is invited, me included.
Remind me to ring Anders on Saturday, the week after his surgery, to see how the shoulder is.
Irina is struggling with the recovery after her hysterectomy. She's back at her mum's and says the tiredness is the worst part. Her follow-up appointment is in a fortnight.

Afua and Jamal are going to the Adele concert in Hyde Park next summer. They booked the tickets for their tenth anniversary, which is the same weekend, and they're making a proper trip of it with a hotel and a fancy dinner the night before. Afua's mum is having the kids. Jamal says it cost a fortune but it's worth it.
Picked up the race pack for Sunday. Start is at 8, so I'll need to be at the bus by 6:30.
Laura texted after the last night. The play sold out on Saturday and the director wants her for the spring production too.
Hoang Zhou from accounts has a vasectomy booked for Friday and has asked everyone not to make jokes. Fat chance.
Bogdan's wife Natasha is twenty weeks along. They found out it's a girl at the scan on Monday, and her brother Mihai is already planning to teach the baby chess.
Don't forget to send Lwazi a card for the new baby. Little Anika was born on Thursday, and he says Afua is doing brilliantly.

Ayo is taking his nephew to his first football match on Saturday, Arsenal at home. The lad has just come through a year of chemo and this was the one thing he asked for. Ayo's sister Amara is anxious about crowds and infections, so they've got seats in the family stand. I need to ask Ayo afterwards how the day went.
Siobhan's mum, Dr Morris, is retiring from the hospital next month after thirty-five years on the maternity ward. There's a do for her on the Friday before she finishes.
Chris loves vintage cars and is restoring a 1972 Mini in his garage. He mentioned he'd love a proper set of spanners for Christmas.
Need to pick up Mum's prescription on the way home tomorrow and drop it round before her physio at 2.
Gareth's daughter Amara starts her nursing placement on the children's ward next week. She's thrilled but a bit anxious about the night shifts.
Finn, who everyone calls Finny, had grommets put in on Wednesday and can suddenly hear everything. His mum said he jumped when the kettle boiled.

Long catch-up with Nadia at the café. Her sister Laura is having her second round of IVF next month, so we should keep it low-key. Nadia's own little one, Fern, is christened in a fortnight; Callum's parents are coming over from Dublin the day before and staying until the Tuesday. She asked if I'd be a godparent. I said yes, so I need to find a gift and maybe a reading.
